title: Ivy - KV cache / warmup pocket checklist
content:
Morning pocket notes — quick, ephemeral. Use as personal checklist and scratch during the node warmup window.

Context: Dedicated pool has been flapping for small seq workloads (prod-cold-zone). Wanted: consistent token p50 < 120ms, avoid cold KV misses when autoscaling up. Today's slot: pre-warm low-latency nodes and confirm prefix / KV cache priming.

Top priorities (ordered)
- [ ] Warm up 3 standby pods (gpu-pool-d-*) in us-west-2 before 09:30PT window (estimate 18m)
- [ ] Validate KV cache hitrate >= 92% on warm pods (check two-minute window)
- [ ] Annotate canaries for affinity tests, run lightweight conv-load to confirm stable sequence latency
- [ ] If preemptible spot nodes join, ensure fallback routing to dedicated-reserve pool is enabled

Quick commands (copy-paste)
- Drain target node without evicting daemonsets: kubectl drain ip-10-0-12-45 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=120
- Restart pod with warmup env: kubectl rollout restart deploy/kv-warmup-worker -n dedicated-pool
- Check GPU topology and temp: kubectl exec -it pod/gpu-debug -- nvidia-smi topo --matrix; kubectl exec -it pod/gpu-debug -- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=temperature.gpu,utilization.gpu --format=csv
- Query cache metric (PromQL): sum(rate(redwood_kv_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(redwood_kv_requests_total[5m]))

Warmup script plan (manual steps)
1) Annotate pods for affinity test: kubectl annotate pod <pod> redwood/affinity-test=ivy-warmup --overwrite
2) Kick lightweight priming job (cpu tiny, model shard subset): curl -X POST https://stage.api.redwood.ai/prime -H 'Authorization: Bearer $PRIMING_KEY' -d '{"model":"llama-13b","sequences":30,"tokens":120}'
3) Watch logs: kubectl logs -f deploy/kv-warmup-worker -n dedicated-pool | grep "prefix-cache"
4) Confirm Prometheus shows kv_hit_rate > 0.92 for the 3 pods (tag by pod label affinity=ivy-warmup)

Notes / heuristics I keep forgetting
- Priming with 30 sequences of ~120 tokens tends to cover both short and medium prefix caches (good tradeoff between token cost and hitrate).
- If batch size auto-tunes down after warmup, check the NNGA controller for batch_policy=aggressive; sometimes it reduces throughput unexpectedly.
- GPUs cold-start cost is roughly 600ms for nvlink init on certain 80GB SKUs — account for that in the 09:30 SLA window.

Contingency / rollback checklist
- If p50 jumps > 200ms after warmup: mark the rollout paused (redwood console -> rollout -> pause), scale down warmup replicas to 0, and route traffic to last-known-good model variant (model:v2026-03-04).
- If KV hitrate stays < 80%: kill warmup job, clear cache on the offending pod(s) by restarting process, re-run priming with payload reduced to shorter seqs for faster iteration.

Open questions / TODOs to follow up later
- Can we push a tiny priming mode that uses smaller memory footprint but hits head prefixes faster? (ask Meera)
- Confirm whether autoscaler respects pod annotations we use for affinity tests (might be ignored by cluster-autoscaler). Filed PLAT-3217 but need verification.
- Experiment: try increasing prefix-cache size on one canary GPU to test hitrate delta (small perf risk).

Signals / dashboards to glance at after warmup
- redwood_kv_hit_rate by pod -> want steady >92%
- per-pod token latency p50/p95 -> compare warm vs cold pods
- node preemption events (cloudprovider logs) -> if spikes, switch to reserved routing

Personal timing and reminders
- 09:05 — start annotating and kicking priming jobs
- 09:22 — check first hitrate snapshot, log results to slack #platform-warmup (quick note)
- 09:40 — final check before traffic ramp (if not green, hold ramp and escalate)

Random scratch (notes to self)
- Slack snippet for quick status: "Ivy: warmup started for 3 pods in us-west-2; priming sequences running; will update at ~09:22PT. If preemption events spike, fallback to reserved pool is enabled. - Ivy"
- Quick mental checklist before leaving desk: did I leave a rolling restart running? Any priming keys leaked in terminal history? Clear bash history for the session.

End of pocket notes. Will convert to a formal runbook if this sequence becomes repetitive or is used for oncall playbook.
